title: Constant degrees multiply for finite locally free morphisms
statement: Let $X,Y,S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $r,s\geq0$ be integers, and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to S$ be finite locally free morphisms of constant degrees $r$ and $s$, respectively [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Then $g\circ f:X\to S$ is finite locally free of constant degree $rs$. No reducedness, Noetherian, connectedness or separability hypothesis is imposed; empty schemes and degree zero are allowed.

source.place: Tag 02KC, lemma-composition-finite-locally-free, with its constant-degree refinement using Tag 02KA, definition-finite-locally-free, and fibre ranks; Tag 02KB, lemma-finite-flat. The rank calculation reduces over each finite fibre algebra to Algebra Tag 02M9, lemma-locally-free-semi-local-free, literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex.

proof.text: The composite $h=g\circ f$ is finite locally free by [lem-trf-finite-locally-free-composition]. It remains to compute its fibre dimension at an arbitrary point $z\in S$.

Choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $z$, and put $U=g^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ and $W=f^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}C_0$. These inverse images are affine by the definition of a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Restrictions to target opens preserve the finite locally free condition and the stated degrees: the finite, flat and locally finitely presented conditions are local conditions, and the fibres are unchanged. Put $K=\kappa(z)$, $B=B_0\otimes_AK$ and $C=C_0\otimes_AK$. The affine fibre-product theorem [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $Y_z$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $X_z$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C$, with their map induced by $B\to C$. In particular $\dim_KB=s$ by the degree hypothesis [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

source.place: Tag 02KA, definition-finite-locally-free; Tag 02KB, lemma-finite-flat. Affine fibre products: Schemes Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-finite-locally-free-principal-basis-cover] to $W\to U$: choose $t_1,\ldots,t_m\in B_0$ generating the unit ideal and isomorphisms $(C_0)_{t_i}\cong(B_0)_{t_i}^{\oplus r}$. Write $\bar t_i$ for the images in $B$. These still generate the unit ideal, by applying $B_0\to B$ to an equation $\sum a_it_i=1$. Extension of scalars gives $C\cong C_0\otimes_{B_0}B$, by $c\otimes(b\otimes k)\mapsto cb\otimes k$ with inverse $c\otimes k\mapsto c\otimes(1\otimes k)$. Localizing this formula and the chosen basis isomorphisms gives $C_{\bar t_i}\cong(C_0)_{t_i}\otimes_{(B_0)_{t_i}}B_{\bar t_i}\cong B_{\bar t_i}^{\oplus r}$. The localization comparison sends $(c/t_i^a)\otimes(b/\bar t_i^b)$ to $cb/\bar t_i^{a+b}$ and is inverted using the localization universal property. Tensoring the basis map and its inverse gives inverse maps, since each acts on the displayed basis coordinates. Thus $C$ has a finite principal-open free cover of constant rank $r$ as a $B$-module.

source.place: Elementary extension of the principal-basis charts of Morphisms Tag 02KB; tensor and localization universal properties.

proof.text: Since $B$ is finite-dimensional over $K$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian] makes it Artinian; [lem-sfb-artinian-spectrum-finite] makes its prime spectrum finite, hence its subset of maximal ideals is finite. Apply [lem-sfb-semilocal-constant-rank-basis] to the cover in step 3. It supplies a $B$-basis $c_1,\ldots,c_r$ of $C$. This application uses neither reducedness of $B$ nor a field structure on $B$.

Choose a $K$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ of $B$. Then the $rs$ products $b_ic_j$ form a $K$-basis of $C$: expand each element uniquely first in the $c_j$, and then each coefficient uniquely in the $b_i$. Uniqueness in these two expansions proves linear independence as well as spanning. Hence $\dim_KC=rs$. By the fibre identifications of step 2 and the definition of degree [def-pc-finite-locally-free], $h$ has degree $rs$ at $z$, and $z$ was arbitrary. If $B=0$, then its unital algebra $C$ is zero and both dimensions are zero; if $r=0$, the empty $B$-basis gives $C=0$. If $S$ is empty there are no points to check. These observations also cover $s=0$ and all empty-source cases.
